profile.reading:
Per NTT's own Global Data Centers facility page, this building, NTT Ashburn VA5, is located at 21583 Megawatt Dr., Ashburn, VA 20147, the fifth of nine planned buildings on NTT's 224-megawatt, 78-acre Ashburn campus in Loudoun County's "Data Center Alley." The operator publishes 140,000 square feet of data floor space and 32 megawatts of critical IT load for this specific building; no formal certifications or opening year are stated on the page. NTT's own site lists an identical street address, square footage, and MW figure for the neighboring VA4 building, indicating VA4 and VA5 are twin buildings or pods sharing one campus address rather than a data error in this registry.

Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to every Ashburn-area facility. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates that will raise a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers effective January 1, 2027. Under the new rules, data center customers with 25 megawatts or more of demand, a threshold this single building already exceeds on its own, must sign 14-year mandatory contracts, pay a minimum 85% of transmission and distribution costs and a minimum 60% of generation costs regardless of actual usage, and post collateral upfront for grid upgrades, per Inside Climate News's reporting on the SCC decision.

NTT's US Global Data Centers footprint spans seven named campuses in total: Ashburn, Virginia at 224 megawatts; Chicago, Illinois at more than 200 megawatts; Dallas, Texas at 160 megawatts; Hillsboro, Oregon at 126 megawatts; Phoenix, Arizona at 240 megawatts; and a combined Sacramento/Santa Clara, California figure of 68 megawatts, totaling roughly 1,118 megawatts or more of disclosed US capacity, per the operator's own locations page. The US business operates under the NTT DATA Global Data Centers Americas name, the successor brand to RagingWire Data Centers, now under Japan's NTT DATA Group and parent Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, a Tokyo Stock Exchange-listed company not subject to SEC 10-K filing requirements.

reading.body:
NTT VA5 publishes 32 MW of IT capacity, ranking 13th among 19 Virginia facilities with disclosed power figures and accounting for roughly 2.4 percent of their 1,326 MW combined total.

The conversion of 32 MW to usable infrastructure depends entirely on cooling architecture and rack density, which NTT does not publish. At 40 kW per rack (typical for AI training), this facility holds roughly 800 racks. At 10 kW per rack (enterprise standard), it holds roughly 3,200 racks. This 4x variance matters because AI workloads concentrate at the higher power density, but published data cannot determine which applies here. The operator publishes no cooling architecture, power-usage-effectiveness figure, or rack count.

VA5 sits on Megawatt Drive in Ashburn, a corridor with established power delivery and fiber density. This location advantage is real but does not reveal the actual binding constraint: whether utility power allocation or interconnection capacity is available for expansion, and whether the 32 MW figure represents full buildout or a phase of a larger project. Virginia leads US data center concentration, meaning this mid-tier asset competes with much larger neighbors for the same power supply and tenant demand.

The operator publishes no certifications or compliance credentials for the facility. Across 326 Virginia data centers mapped in OpenStreetMap, most publish no capacity data at all, so the 1,326 MW total for this state is a lower bound on actual footprint by an unknown margin.
